squawks.headline: ECB's Escrivá says he is optimistic about AI and sees large productivity gains
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá made the remarks on Monday, in the same set of comments in which he called AI valuations clearly high.

squawks.headline: ECB's Escrivá says AI valuations are clearly high
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said valuations linked to artificial intelligence are obviously elevated. The comment came on the same day as his other remarks on rates and inflation.

squawks.headline: ECB's Escrivá says markets have been fairly insensitive to price risk in recent years
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá made the remark on Monday, in further comments alongside his earlier statements on rates and inflation.

squawks.headline: ECB's Escrivá says rates at 2% are a reasonable level to hold inflation around 2%
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said a policy rate of 2% is reasonable for keeping inflation at around 2%.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says the current inflation episode cannot be compared with 2022 as the macro backdrop is very different
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said inflation is clearly above the ECB's objective, but that the current macroeconomic situation differs greatly from 2022 and the two periods are not comparable.

squawks.headline: Oil flows through Kazakhstan's Atyrau-Samara pipeline are halted
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that oil flows on the Atyrau-Samara pipeline from Kazakhstan have stopped. It gave no cause and no expected duration.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says inflation is well above the 2% target but the impact on the wider economy is moderate for now
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said inflation is clearly above the ECB's 2% objective. He said the effect on the broader economy has so far been fairly moderate.

squawks.headline: ECB's Escrivá says the oil and gas price shock is bigger than expected but there are no signs yet of second-round effects
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said the energy price shock had proved larger than expected. He added that second-round effects on inflation had not yet appeared.

squawks.headline: ECB's Escrivá says the outlook for interest rates is highly complex
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member José Luis Escrivá said the rates scenario is marked by high complexity. He gave no figures.

squawks.headline: ECB's Escrivá says a lack of fiscal adjustment is not limited to France
squawks.detail: Bank of Spain Governor Escrivá said the absence of fiscal adjustment extends beyond France. He spoke on the same day as other ECB policymakers' comments on French public finances.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says France will very probably get a budget and markets may be overreacting to the French situation
squawks.detail: Bank of France Governor Moulin said France's budget position is poor and must be dealt with. He also said the country is very likely to pass a budget and that markets may be overreacting.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says France's situation is a cause for concern and markets are worried about it
squawks.detail: Bank of France Governor Moulin, an ECB Governing Council member, said markets are concerned about the situation in France. He also said rises in global interest rates affect every country.

squawks.headline: US construction spending falls 1.9% on the month, against a forecast 0.3% rise
squawks.detail: US construction spending fell 1.9% month on month, compared with a forecast rise of 0.3% and a previous reading of 0.9%.

squawks.headline: US October ISM manufacturing index rises to 55.5, above the 54.5 forecast, as prices paid ease to 75.2
squawks.detail: The US ISM October manufacturing index came in at 55.5, against a forecast of 54.5 and 54.5 the previous month. New orders were 55.5 (forecast 55, previous 55.3), employment was 52.4 (forecast 52, previous 52.7) and prices paid were 75.2 (forecast 77.2, previous 77.9).

squawks.headline: US Gulf allies are preparing for a new round of strikes on Iran and possible retaliation, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that America's Gulf allies are getting ready for further US strikes on Iran and for the blowback that could follow. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US final October manufacturing PMI is revised down to 54.9 from the 56.0 flash reading
squawks.detail: S&P Global's final US manufacturing PMI for October came in at 54.9, below the 56.0 flash estimate and forecast. September's reading was 55.9.

squawks.headline: UK 10-year gilt yield heads for its largest one-day drop since 20 May
squawks.detail: A market report says the 10-year gilt yield is on course for its biggest single-day fall since 20 May.

squawks.headline: Canada's October manufacturing PMI drops to 49.6 from 51.5
squawks.detail: Canada's manufacturing PMI came in at 49.6, down from 51.5 previously. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve falls to 282.2m barrels, its lowest level since 1982
squawks.detail: Crude stocks in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.2 million barrels last week, the lowest level since 1982.

squawks.headline: Iran's Foreign Minister says Hormuz will reopen and talks resume if the US accepts Tehran's conditions, otherwise the status quo continues
squawks.detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said Tehran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz are clear. If the US accepts them, the strait will reopen and negotiations will resume; if not, the current situation will continue. State news agency IRNA reported the remarks.

squawks.headline: Iran's Foreign Minister says talks via Qatari and Pakistani mediators are intensive and warns of a harsher response to any new strikes
squawks.detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said Tehran has presented its terms and plan and that reopening the Strait of Hormuz depends on Iran's conditions being accepted, according to IRNA. He said Iran is ready to work with the US if it chooses honest diplomacy, and that any deception or military operations would meet a harsher response than before.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says Tehran will seek to settle the war with the US through dialogue
squawks.detail: Iranian state media reported the comments from President Pezeshkian on the conflict with the US.

squawks.headline: China's Foreign Minister calls for regional energy and shipping lane security to be safeguarded
squawks.detail: China's Foreign Minister made the call amid the Middle East conflict and disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

squawks.headline: Brent drops to a fresh intraday low near $106 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent was reported trading near $106 a barrel at its intraday low on Monday afternoon. Earlier on Monday it had fallen 3% to $108.34 as hopes grew for an end to the US-Iran conflict.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian rejects what he calls false claims and excessive demands from Iran's enemies
squawks.detail: Iranian state outlet Press TV reported the remarks by President Pezeshkian on Monday, as efforts to restart US-Iran talks continue.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian says the Supreme Leader has given the government some powers over negotiations
squawks.detail: Iran's ISNA news agency reported the remarks by President Pezeshkian. They come as efforts to restart US-Iran talks continue.

squawks.headline: UK October manufacturing PMI shows the strongest output growth in more than two years, alongside fast-rising costs
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the October manufacturing survey published on Monday showed British factory output growing at its fastest pace in more than two years, with input costs rising quickly. The survey comes in the same week as the Bank of England's rate decision.

squawks.headline: India tells liquor firms it will honour the India-UK trade pact and settle the Scotch tariff dispute, sources say
squawks.detail: According to sources, India told a meeting with the drinks industry that bulk Scotch imports are among the concessions in the India-UK trade deal and that it will resolve the tariff dispute.

squawks.headline: Vitol CEO warns of a potentially difficult spring for oil and says demand will need a year to get back to 2025 levels
squawks.detail: Vitol's chief executive made the further comments on the outlook for the oil market on Monday, after his earlier remarks on demand, inventories and spare capacity.

squawks.headline: Vitol CEO says oil demand will be about 3m bpd lower by end-2026 and the system has low inventories and no spare capacity
squawks.detail: The Vitol chief executive said oil demand will take a year to get back to its 2025 level and that the world could not cope with a bigger disruption than the current one. He also said the market could face a difficult spring.

squawks.headline: European gas prices drop as much as 5.3% to €98.49/MWh
squawks.detail: European benchmark gas fell by up to 5.3% to €98.49/MWh on Monday, according to a market wire report. The move came as Brent was also reported trading lower.

squawks.headline: PBOC cuts its stock buyback relending rate to 1% from 1.25%
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China lowered the rate on its stock buyback relending facility to 1% from 1.25%.

squawks.headline: Equinor CEO says European industrial gas demand is 30% below its five-year average
squawks.detail: Equinor's chief executive said demand for natural gas from European industry is running 30% below the five-year average.

squawks.headline: Equinor CEO says shipping costs have changed rapidly and the efficient market of the past is gone
squawks.detail: The Equinor chief executive said shipping costs have shifted quickly and that the efficient market the industry was used to no longer exists. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Israel's Netanyahu urges Trump to carry out new strikes on Iran
squawks.detail: A wire headline reports that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is pressing US President Trump for renewed military strikes against Iran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Equinor CEO says Europe enters winter more vulnerable than usual, with gas storage at its lowest in 15 years
squawks.detail: The Equinor chief executive said European gas storage is at the lowest level the company has seen in 15 years, leaving the region more exposed than normal going into winter. He also said more customers are seeking long-term Norwegian gas contracts, with pipeline gas deals now running to 15 years and beyond.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says the Budget keeps Local Housing Allowance frozen into 2027-28, affecting over a million families
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation said the Local Housing Allowance freeze is extended into 2027-28, leaving more than a million families worse off, 91% of them in the bottom half of the income distribution. It said the Budget's Your First Home scheme will help a small number of renters buy.

squawks.headline: TotalEnergies CEO says Europe will not face a gas shortage this winter
squawks.detail: The chief executive of TotalEnergies said he expects no shortfall in European gas supply over the coming winter.

squawks.headline: Trump says oil rose less than he expected during the Iran war and predicts US petrol prices will drop below $2 a gallon
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the comments on 2 November and also said the US is receiving millions of barrels of oil from Venezuela. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: ECB's Makhlouf says the French government must repair its public finances
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Makhlouf said on Monday that France needs to put its public finances in order. The post reported no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Trump says Iran wants a deal with the US but it remains to be seen whether one is reached
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Iran in comments reported on 2 November, and also said the US has knocked out two of Iran's regimes. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: China proposes looser foreign exchange rules for current account transactions
squawks.detail: Chinese authorities have put forward proposals to ease foreign exchange rules on current account transactions. The post gave no further details.

squawks.headline: Gazprom's daily gas exports to China through Power of Siberia reach a record
squawks.detail: Gazprom's daily gas exports to China through the Power of Siberia pipeline have hit a record high, according to a market news post. The post gave no volume.

squawks.headline: Russian Foreign Ministry voices extreme concern over signals that new military action against Iran is planned
squawks.detail: Russia's Foreign Ministry said signs of planned fresh military action against Iran were causing it extreme concern, Tass reported. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Belgian PM De Wever offers resignation after budget talks fail; King holds decision in reserve
squawks.detail: The Belgian Royal Palace says Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his resignation after budget negotiations failed. The King has not yet decided and will begin consultations with majority party leaders tomorrow.

squawks.headline: ECB's Vujcic names AI valuations as a financial stability risk and says sovereign bond markets need monitoring
squawks.detail: ECB Vice-President Vujcic said AI valuations are among the risks set out in the ECB's financial stability review. He also said the sovereign bond market must be monitored.

squawks.headline: IRGC says 11 tankers have burned in the Strait of Hormuz since 25 October
squawks.detail: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps gave a count of 11 tankers burned in the Strait of Hormuz since 25 October. No market reaction was reported with the statement.

squawks.headline: China's Wang Yi urges all sides in the Middle East conflict to pursue political solutions rather than renewed fighting
squawks.detail: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi made the call on Monday during a meeting in Beijing with an Iranian national security official, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: UK 30-year gilt yield falls more than 7bp on the day to 5.648%, its lowest since 7 August
squawks.detail: The 30-year gilt yield dropped by more than 7bp on the day to 5.648%, its lowest level since 7 August, according to a market report. Earlier, the 10-year yield fell 5bp to 5.23%.

squawks.headline: UAE energy minister declines to give current oil export levels and says the country will be better prepared whatever happens in the war
squawks.detail: The UAE's energy and infrastructure minister would not say how much oil the country is exporting now. He said the course of the war cannot be predicted but the UAE will be more prepared than before.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says current conditions on the ground rule out restoring Russian gas flows to Europe via Ukraine for now
squawks.detail: The Kremlin was responding to a WSJ report that the US is pushing to restore Russian gas transit to Europe through Ukraine as part of a Moscow-Kyiv energy truce.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says no further humanitarian ceasefires like Oleshky are planned so far, after Ukraine accuses Russia of regrouping
squawks.detail: Ukraine's General Staff said Russian forces used last week's humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky to reinforce their positions. The Kremlin replied that both sides could regroup during a ceasefire and called this normal practice.

squawks.headline: UK final October manufacturing PMI confirmed at 52.8, in line with forecast and the previous reading
squawks.detail: The final UK manufacturing PMI came in at 52.8, matching both the 52.8 forecast and the prior figure.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says OBR forecasts make the 2020s the weakest decade for income growth on record
squawks.detail: Citing the latest OBR forecasts, the Resolution Foundation says incomes will finish 2030 only 1.4 per cent above their 2020 level.

squawks.headline: Kyiv says Russia has resumed attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region now that the truce has ended
squawks.detail: According to Ukrainian authorities, Russian attacks on the Kherson region restarted after the truce expired.

squawks.headline: Brent's fall widens to 4% as hopes build for an end to the US-Iran conflict
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reports that Brent crude is down 4%, more than the 3% intraday fall recorded earlier. It links the drop to growing hopes that the US-Iran conflict can be resolved.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kazimir says waiting for inflation to rise before acting is unwise and markets may not fully grasp the path ahead
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazimir said action is needed before high inflation becomes entrenched, and that waiting for firms to pass on costs would be a mistake. He also said markets may not fully understand the policy path that is needed.

squawks.headline: UK 10-year gilt yield falls 5bp to 5.23%, its lowest level since September 2023
squawks.detail: Market reports say the 10-year gilt yield fell 5bp to 5.23%, the lowest level since September 2023.

squawks.headline: PBOC says 31 firms applied for its swap facility, with an allotment of 100bn yuan
squawks.detail: China's central bank said 31 firms had applied to its swap facility for securities, fund and insurance firms, with 100bn yuan allotted.

squawks.headline: PBOC to run swap facility operations for securities, fund and insurance firms on 3 November
squawks.detail: China's central bank said it will carry out swap facility operations for securities firms, fund managers and insurers on 3 November.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kazimir says the debate is now about how much further ECB action is needed, not whether it is
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Peter Kazimir said further policy action is increasingly a question of scale rather than whether it will happen.

squawks.headline: Eurozone final October manufacturing PMI is revised up to 52.7, above the 52.4 forecast and flash reading
squawks.detail: The final eurozone manufacturing PMI for October came in at 52.7. The forecast and the previous reading were both 52.4.

squawks.headline: Germany's final October manufacturing PMI is confirmed at 54.2, in line with forecast
squawks.detail: The final German manufacturing PMI for October was 54.2. This matches both the forecast and the previous reading.

squawks.headline: Brent falls 3% intraday to $108.34 a barrel and WTI drops below $99
squawks.detail: Brent crude was reported down 3.00% intraday at $108.34 a barrel, with WTI also down 3.00% and trading below $99 a barrel.

squawks.headline: France's final October manufacturing PMI comes in at 49.5, above the 49.3 forecast
squawks.detail: France's final manufacturing PMI for October was 49.5, against a forecast and prior reading of 49.3, and remains below the 50 mark that separates expansion from contraction.

squawks.headline: Iran says the US must change its approach for talks to go ahead and nuclear negotiations have not yet been reached
squawks.detail: Iran said the US needs to change its approach before talks can proceed, and that it is not yet at the point of nuclear negotiations with Washington. Foreign ministry spokesperson Baghaei said Iran's seven-step proposal remains the basis for diplomacy and could be put into effect over two days.

squawks.headline: Spain's October manufacturing PMI rises to 52.2, above the 50.5 forecast
squawks.detail: Spain's manufacturing PMI came in at 52.2, against a forecast of 50.5 and a previous reading of 51.0.

squawks.headline: Iran says a letter from US Vice President Vance gives no new basis for talks and its demands have not changed
squawks.detail: Iran's response to the letter from US Vice President Vance was reported in a market headline. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Poland's October manufacturing PMI rises to 50.0, above the 49.4 forecast; Hungary's reading is 53.1
squawks.detail: Poland's manufacturing purchasing managers' index came in at 50.0 for October, against a forecast of 49.4. Hungary's manufacturing PMI for October was 53.1.

squawks.headline: Start of US-Iran negotiations depends on the naval blockade ending, report says
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that opening negotiations between Iran and the US is conditional on an end to the naval blockade; the post does not name the source of the statement. No market reaction is reported.

squawks.headline: Draft proposal from the Doha talks goes out for feedback and a follow-up meeting is possible, source says; Iranian negotiators have left
squawks.detail: An official briefed on the Doha talks said a draft proposal has been circulated for feedback and that a follow-up meeting is possible. A separate source said Iranian negotiators left Doha on Sunday and that their departure was not caused by problems in the talks.

squawks.headline: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz cannot reopen until US sanctions are lifted
squawks.detail: Iran said on Monday that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen before US sanctions are lifted. The statement came as efforts to restart US-Iran talks continued.

squawks.headline: Iran says it is still exchanging messages with the US and has set out its demands, with a deputy foreign minister in Doha
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei says message exchanges with the US are continuing and that Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi was in Doha to help them along. Iran also says it has passed what it calls legitimate demands to the US.

squawks.headline: Iran says its seven-step proposal underpins diplomacy with the US and could be implemented within days
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Baghaei said Iran's seven-step proposal is the basis for its diplomacy with the US. He said there is a chance it could be implemented over the next few days.

squawks.headline: German real retail sales fall 2% in September, against a 0.4% rise forecast
squawks.detail: German real retail sales dropped 2% month on month in September, after a 1.3% rise the previous month. They were down 2.3% year on year, compared with a -0.2% forecast and -0.4% previously.

squawks.headline: Goldman Sachs now expects a 25bp BoE rate rise in February 2027 on top of a quarter-point hike next week
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Goldman Sachs has added a February 25bp Bank of England rate rise to its forecast, alongside its existing call for a quarter-point increase next week. The bank cited higher energy prices and stronger economic data.

squawks.headline: ADNOC CEO says Hormuz disruption has taken nearly 1bn barrels out of global inventories
squawks.detail: ADNOC's chief executive said disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has drawn global inventories down by nearly 1 billion barrels and the world has used up its available supply reserves. He added that some markets report diesel stocks at their weakest seasonal levels in 35 years.

squawks.headline: BoJ Governor Ueda has all but locked in a December rate rise, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda has all but committed to a rate rise in December. The report says investors remain uncertain how much further the BoJ could tighten once rates near neutral.

squawks.headline: China's Xi warns against the Middle East and Gulf becoming a battleground for great power rivalry
squawks.detail: China's President Xi said, according to state broadcaster CCTV, that China will keep pursuing political and diplomatic settlement of disputes. He also said Beijing is willing to step up dialogue and cooperation with Arab nations to restore regional peace and stability soon.

squawks.headline: BoJ says rate rises should ease inflation and support consumption, and notes higher real yields at the long end
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan says underlying inflation has risen to about 2% and is becoming embedded at that level. It also says real interest rates have climbed recently, especially for long and super-long maturities, while median real rates stay low, and that it is watching equity and currency moves as part of a broad review of financial conditions.

squawks.headline: Brent drops to $109.52 in Asian trade, heading for its lowest level in more than a week; WTI nears $100
squawks.detail: Brent was reported down more than $3 at $110.37 a barrel. It then fell nearly 2% more to $109.52, while WTI dropped about 2% towards $100 after earlier sliding more than $3 to $101.11.

squawks.headline: US pushes to restore Russian gas flows to Europe through Ukraine as part of a Moscow-Kyiv energy truce, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Washington is seeking to resume Russian gas shipments to Europe via Ukraine. The aim is an energy truce between Russia and Ukraine.

squawks.headline: China's RatingDog manufacturing PMI eases to 52.0 in October, above the 51.6 forecast
squawks.detail: China's RatingDog manufacturing PMI fell to 52.0 in October from 52.1 in September. The forecast was 51.6.

squawks.headline: Brent and WTI fall a further $2 a barrel in Asian trade as efforts to restart Middle East talks gather pace
squawks.detail: Brent and WTI crude were each reported down $2 a barrel early on Monday. The WSJ linked the fall to efforts to get Middle East parties back to negotiations, and Reuters said high oil prices were limiting demand for sovereign bonds as a safe haven.

squawks.headline: Japan's Katayama says the US-Japan FX statement still applies and Tokyo will act against disorderly moves
squawks.detail: Japan's finance minister Satsuki Katayama said the joint currency statement with the US remains in force and that stable FX markets are crucial. She declined to comment on specific yen levels and said Prime Minister Takaichi sees yen weakness as a problem.

squawks.headline: South Korea and Taiwan October manufacturing PMIs fall; Japan's final reading holds at 53.3
squawks.detail: S&P Global's October manufacturing PMI fell to 51.3 from 53.9 in South Korea and to 54.9 from 56.7 in Taiwan. Japan's final reading was unchanged from the flash estimate at 53.3.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is very near a trade deal with Canada after Carney reports a good call on trade
squawks.detail: Canadian Prime Minister Carney said on Sunday he had a good conversation with President Trump on future trade between the two countries, which have been in a trade war. Trump said a deal with Canada was very near and also said he had held a productive discussion with Israel's Netanyahu that covered Iran.

squawks.headline: US-Iran talks make positive progress and mediators work to close remaining gaps, Axios reports; oil falls more than 1%
squawks.detail: Axios cited a diplomat involved in the US-Iran talks as saying talks had progressed positively and mediators were working on the remaining differences. Oil prices were later reported down more than 1% as the Iran-Qatar talks sought to end the US-Iran war.

squawks.headline: US approves $2.1bn sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the US has approved a $2.1bn sale of Patriot interceptors to Ukraine. President Zelenskyy had accused the Trump administration of holding up the weapons as relations between the two countries worsened.

squawks.headline: Lavrov says core US-Russia issues remain unresolved as sanctions stay in place and arms keep flowing to Ukraine
squawks.detail: Russia's foreign minister said sanctions are still in force and weapons are still being supplied to Ukraine. He also said it is unclear what Ukraine will bring to new settlement talks, and called Zelenskiy's references to long-range strikes unhelpful.

squawks.headline: Poland's Sikorski calls for a Black Sea ceasefire and ties any Russian energy sales to Europe to a fair end to the Ukraine war
squawks.detail: Polish Foreign Minister Sikorski said G20 members discussed food security, freedom of navigation and energy. He said Poland wants a Black Sea ceasefire so Ukrainian and Russian food supplies can be shipped out, and that the war in Ukraine must end fairly if Russia wants to sell energy to Europe again.

squawks.headline: Lavrov says Russia's stance is unchanged ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Moscow's position had not changed before the negotiations in Abu Dhabi. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Fourth tanker explodes after striking a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's IRGC says via state broadcaster
squawks.detail: Iran's IRGC, as reported by Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, says a fourth tanker exploded after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC says the tanker had ignored warnings not to use an 'unauthorised route' through the strait.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is not considering lifting sanctions on Russia's sovereign wealth fund
squawks.detail: US President Trump says lifting sanctions on Russia's sovereign wealth fund is not under consideration.

squawks.headline: Trump says talks with Iran are continuing and the US is in no hurry
squawks.detail: US President Trump says talks with Iran are ongoing and that the US has time. He also says the US is spending very little money on Iran.

squawks.headline: Canadian dollar reaches six-week high against the US dollar as higher oil prices support bets on more Bank of Canada tightening
squawks.detail: Reuters reports the Canadian dollar extended its monthly gain on Friday as the oil price jump lifted expectations that the Bank of Canada will tighten further. The move outweighed weaker-than-expected Canadian GDP data.

squawks.headline: White House pushes back hearing on mortgage fraud allegations against Fed Governor Cook to December, Hassett says
squawks.detail: Kevin Hassett, President Trump's top economic adviser, said the White House hearing into mortgage fraud allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook has been delayed until December, Reuters reports. On Friday, Cook's lawyers would not confirm that any date had been agreed.

squawks.headline: Qatari mediators hold 12 hours of talks in Tehran aimed at securing a US-Iran deal, Axios reports
squawks.detail: Axios reports that Qatari negotiators spent 12 hours in talks in Tehran trying to unlock a deal between the US and Iran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Treasury report finds the blockade and sanctions are crippling Iran's economy, Axios reports
squawks.detail: Axios cites a US Treasury report saying the US blockade and sanctions are inflicting severe damage on Iran's economy. The report adds to the running US-Iran pressure campaign story.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle up 2.4% at $117.64 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures settled $2.76 higher at $117.64 a barrel, a gain of 2.4%.

squawks.headline: US orders non-emergency government staff to leave Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks on airports and infrastructure
squawks.detail: The US embassy in Riyadh said on Friday that non-emergency government employees and their families have been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia, effective 23 October, because of safety risks, Reuters reports. The embassy cited Houthi attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure.

squawks.headline: WTI crude futures settle up 2.08% at $104.12 a barrel
squawks.detail: NYMEX December WTI crude futures settled $2.12 higher at $104.12 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.7905 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.3120 a gallon.

squawks.headline: Gilts rally with core bonds in a risk-off move as sterling holds steady
squawks.detail: A UK market commentator reports that gilts are rallying alongside other core government bonds amid risk-off trading on Friday, with sterling steady. No yield levels were given.

squawks.headline: Pakistan's military says it is cautiously optimistic about its Iran-US mediation
squawks.detail: The Pakistani military spokesman spoke to Reuters on Friday in his first interview since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week.

squawks.headline: Fed's Logan says the Fed needs at least two more 25bp rate hikes, after which a pause would be reasonable
squawks.detail: Dallas Fed President Logan said policy should move gradually and stay moderately restrictive, and called it unacceptable for inflation not to return to the 2% target. She said a pause after 50bp of increases would be reasonable, that growth is robust, that the labour market is balanced and may be tightening slightly, and that higher long-term rates have weighed on the economy less than expected.

squawks.headline: Carney says Canada's alliance with the EU will make its financial sector more competitive
squawks.detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the new strategic alliance with the EU will boost the competitiveness of the financial sector. He spoke after Canada and the EU signed a political agreement on a digital trade deal.

squawks.headline: Carney says Canada will contribute €500m to the EU's Ukraine support loan
squawks.detail: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a €500m contribution to the EU's loan for Ukraine. This follows the earlier EU-Canada agreement on Canada joining the loan.

squawks.headline: Von der Leyen says the EU and Canada have agreed that Canada will take part in the EU's loan for Ukraine
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen said Canada's participation in the EU loan for Ukraine has been agreed. Earlier, a joint statement said Canada wanted to join the €90bn support loan.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says he is focused on preventing second-round inflation effects, such as in services
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said his focus is on stopping inflation from feeding through in second-round effects, naming the service sector as an example.

squawks.headline: UK approves a 2 gigawatt undersea power cable
squawks.detail: A market news account reported that the UK has given approval for a 2 gigawatt undersea electricity cable. The post did not give further details.

squawks.headline: Budget includes a fiscal devolution roadmap promising fundamental change to mayoral funding, Institute for Government says
squawks.detail: In a commentary piece, the Institute for Government calls the roadmap the main reform in the budget. It says the roadmap sets out a fundamental change in how mayors are funded.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says public understanding of how the Fed thinks matters, and policy rules are useful for monetary policy
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem also said that communication is not necessarily the same thing as forward guidance. He made the remarks in further comments on Friday afternoon.

squawks.headline: Canada seeks to take part in the EU's €90bn support loan for Ukraine, joint statement says
squawks.detail: A joint Canada-EU statement says Canada is set to contribute to the EU's €90bn loan to Ukraine. The two sides also launched a new alliance that includes deals on minerals and AI.

squawks.headline: Carney says Canada aims to be the EU's first associate member, with talks to be concluded at June European Council meetings
squawks.detail: Canada's Prime Minister Carney said he has accepted European Council President Costa's invitation to attend the June meetings to conclude negotiations, and that the substance, scale and scope of the new form of membership will be set over the coming months. He described it as the deepest possible partnership short of accession, and said a new Canada-EU competition agreement is being concluded alongside the digital trade deal.

squawks.headline: Canada and EU sign political agreement on digital trade deal as Carney launches strategic alliance
squawks.detail: Canada and the European Union signed a political agreement on an EU-Canada digital trade agreement and agreed a strategic alliance, leaving the definition of their new relationship until 2027. Canadian Prime Minister Carney called it a historic day and said the world is becoming more dangerous and divided.

squawks.headline: Canada and EU agree to define by 2027 summit an 'ever-closer association' for Canada that stops short of membership
squawks.detail: The commitment is in a joint statement issued at the EU-Canada summit. The statement was signed by Prime Minister Carney, European Council President Costa and Commission President von der Leyen.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says the Fed will raise rates again soon, and earlier hikes lower the risk to the wider economy
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said inflation is still elevated with risks tilted to the upside, policy and financial conditions remain accommodative, and gradual moves are better than sudden ones. He also said higher expected policy rates are driving elevated long-term bond yields, while inflation expectations are steady and the economy and labour market are robust.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says AI adoption is still at a fairly early stage, and the scale and timing of its economy-wide impact are very uncertain
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane added this point to his earlier remarks on AI and the euro area economy. He did not mention interest rates.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says AI is lifting euro area activity, with AI-related price pressures visible but limited effect on headline inflation
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Lane said artificial intelligence is driving growth and credit trends and could significantly raise productivity, and that AI companies are more sensitive to monetary policy. He said AI-related price pressures can be seen but have had limited impact on headline inflation.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Russia and the US are coordinating dates for a three-way meeting in Abu Dhabi in November
squawks.detail: Ushakov said Russia has sent the US its thoughts on dates for the trilateral talks with Ukraine and is waiting for a reply. He said the meeting will be held in Abu Dhabi in November.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly says AI is important to how policymakers think about policy in the near and medium term
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said artificial intelligence is a significant factor in how the Fed approaches policy over the near and medium term.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation puts real per-person public services spending growth at 1.7% a year from 2023-24 to 2028-29
squawks.detail: In its Budget analysis, the Resolution Foundation says day-to-day spending is rising moderately in this Parliament. It puts real per-person growth in public services spending at 1.7% a year between 2023-24 and 2028-29, close to the two latest periods under Conservative governments.

squawks.headline: European Commission proposes Council approval of the remaining €45bn Ukraine loan tranche for 2027
squawks.detail: The European Commission has proposed that the EU Council approve the remaining €45bn of the Ukraine loan for 2027.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says October oil output is above September's, with December diesel export plan due at the end of November
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak says Russian oil production in October was higher than in September. He adds that Russia will set its plan for December diesel exports at the end of November.

squawks.headline: Fitch says the UK budget keeps broad policy continuity but leaves a large delivery challenge, and still expects significant fiscal slippage
squawks.detail: Fitch Ratings says the UK fiscal consolidation plan becomes much harder to deliver from 2027 and expects significant slippage against spending plans. It also sees moderately more policy risk as the next general election approaches.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says attacks on oil refineries will hurt diesel supplies to the global market
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said strikes on Russian oil refineries will have a negative effect on global diesel supply. He had earlier said Ukraine had resumed such strikes.

squawks.headline: Exxon says UAE oil production is back in line with historical output
squawks.detail: Exxon said on Friday that output in the UAE has recovered to levels consistent with its historical production.

squawks.headline: US officials say Thursday's Iran meeting focused on a blockade and economic pressure, not strikes, Axios reports
squawks.detail: Axios cites several US officials as saying more than 20 people attended Thursday's meeting on Iran, which discussed a blockade and economic pressure at length. The officials said strikes remain possible straight after the midterms.

squawks.headline: Exxon estimates half of Russia's refining capacity is offline; CEO sees global refining starting to recover next year, possibly later
squawks.detail: Exxon estimates that half of Russia's refining capacity is out of action. Its chief executive says global refining capacity could start to recover next year but warns it may take longer.

squawks.headline: OBR estimates £3bn-£4bn a year in extra grant needed to return council housebuilding to 1980s levels
squawks.detail: The Office for Budget Responsibility estimates that returning council housebuilding to 1980s levels could need £3bn to £4bn a year of extra grant funding on top of SAHP money, Inside Housing reports.

squawks.headline: China's commerce ministry opposes US FCC curbs on Chinese testing labs and says further countermeasures will follow if the US continues
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry says the FCC vote restricting Chinese testing labs breaches a consensus agreed between the two heads of state and seriously disrupts the stability of global supply chains. It says Beijing had repeatedly proposed talks on a mutual recognition pact but the US stance was extremely negative, and that China will take further countermeasures if the US continues.

squawks.headline: Chevron CEO Wirth says crude oil and refined product prices are elevated worldwide
squawks.detail: Chevron chief executive Mike Wirth said in a CNBC interview that prices for both crude oil and refined products are running high around the world.

squawks.headline: US Chicago PMI falls to 55.3 in October, below 56.0 forecast and down from 58.8
squawks.detail: MNI's Chicago Business Barometer came in at 55.3 for October, short of the 56.0 consensus, after 58.8 in September.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says business demand stays solid, with weakness only in housing and non-profits, and firms plan to pass on price rises
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said businesses describe broad cost pressures and plans to raise prices, adding that consumer spending has been surprisingly resilient given broadly flat incomes. He made the remarks at a business briefing, which has now ended.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says AI investment is driving demand-side inflation that the Fed can lean against, and cost pressures are hitting firms
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the AI investment surge has strained supply chains and that many cost pressures are hitting US businesses. He said years of elevated inflation make it easier for firms to justify price rises, and that consumer spending has held up surprisingly well despite fairly flat incomes.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says the Fed's direction of travel is clear and the open question is the pace, with a gradual approach signalled
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said in a SiriusXM interview that the Fed has signalled a gradual approach. He added that the Fed will see what it learns over the coming period.

squawks.headline: OBR chair Haskel says revised ONS productivity figures leave the UK productivity puzzle unresolved
squawks.detail: OBR Chair Jonathan Haskel made the remarks about the ONS's revised productivity numbers at a Resolution Foundation event on 29 October, the think tank reports.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Ukrainian refinery strikes will not derail upcoming Ukraine talks and will not be raised in Abu Dhabi
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said Russia will not bring up Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries at the upcoming Abu Dhabi meeting. Interfax reported the Kremlin as saying the strikes do not put the negotiations in doubt.

squawks.headline: German flash October CPI slows to 2.8% y/y from 3.3%, below 3% forecast; HICP also 2.8% against 3.1% forecast
squawks.detail: Germany's preliminary October CPI fell 0.2% m/m against a forecast 0.1% rise, after 0.6% in September. Flash HICP dropped 0.1% m/m against a forecast 0.1% rise, and its annual rate slowed from 3.3%.

squawks.headline: US Treasury yields hold most of their losses after US data; 10-year down 6.22bp at 4.927%, 2-year down 7.05bp at 4.586%
squawks.detail: US Treasury yields mostly held their declines after the release of US economic data. The 10-year yield was last 6.22bp lower at 4.927% and the 2-year yield 7.05bp lower at 4.586%.

squawks.headline: Russia plans to extend its diesel export ban, with some exceptions, to the end of January
squawks.detail: Interfax reports that Russia plans to extend the diesel export ban, with certain exceptions, until the end of January. TASS cites Deputy Prime Minister Novak as saying Russia plans to export 510,000 tonnes of diesel in October and 2.15m tonnes in November.

squawks.headline: ECB asks EU leaders to begin the search for a successor to chief economist Lane
squawks.detail: The ECB has asked EU leaders to start the process of finding a successor to Philip Lane on its Executive Board.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novak says Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after a pause, hitting three refineries and a chemical plant
squawks.detail: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Ukrainian drones attacked three Russian oil refineries and one petrochemical complex, with minor damage at one site. He said the attacks resumed after a period of pause.

squawks.headline: Canadian GDP flat m/m in August against 0.2% forecast; StatCan flash estimate points to a 0.1% fall in September
squawks.detail: Statistics Canada said August GDP was unchanged on the month, missing the 0.2% forecast, and July was also flat. Its flash estimate suggests GDP most likely fell 0.1% in September.

squawks.headline: US Q3 employment cost index rises 0.8%, in line with consensus; wages and salaries slow to 0.7% from 0.9%
squawks.detail: US Q3 employment costs rose 0.8%, down from 0.9% in Q2 and matching consensus. Wages and salaries rose 0.7% and benefit costs 0.9%, after 0.9% and 1.0% respectively in Q2.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC says three oil tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Friday; burning supertanker carrying over 2m barrels abandoned
squawks.detail: The IRGC says the latest vessel was the third oil tanker to strike a mine on Friday, and Iranian state broadcaster IRIB says a supertanker holding more than 2 million barrels has been abandoned and is on fire at the mouth of the Strait. Separately, the FT reports that attackers in a speedboat hit a tanker with limpet mines on Thursday, the first such incident since 2019.

squawks.headline: Iranian state media says a supertanker exploded after striking a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's IRIB News said the supertanker hit a mine about an hour before its report, on what it called an unauthorised route through the strait, and Fars also reported the mine strike. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Exxon CEO Woods says Hormuz crude flows are nearing pre-war levels and calls diesel the key crunch point
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, ExxonMobil chief executive Darren Woods said crude moving through the Strait of Hormuz is getting back close to pre-war levels. He named diesel as the main pressure point, saying demand remains high despite available capacity.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC navy says it stopped two oil tankers south of the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said on Friday that two oil tankers were involved in incidents and were stopped south of the Strait of Hormuz. It said the tankers had ignored radio warnings and tried to use what it called an unauthorised route through the waterway, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Kyiv probably could not have attacked Russian oil refineries without European backing
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Ukraine was unlikely to have carried out strikes on Russian oil refineries without support from Europe.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Kyiv is disregarding Trump's calls to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Ushakov said on Friday that Ukraine has not heeded Trump's repeated demands to stop attacking Russian refineries.

squawks.headline: Trump was briefed on Thursday on possible military options in Iran, Fox reports
squawks.detail: Fox reports that US President Trump received a briefing on Thursday on potential military options against Iran.

squawks.headline: Trump says Iran must make a deal and the US needs a guarantee that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon
squawks.detail: In a KCMO radio interview, US President Trump said he expects the Iran war to be wrapped up soon. He also said it is unclear who to talk to on the Iranian side because many of its leaders are gone.

squawks.headline: ECB's Makhlouf calls the current inflation situation uncomfortable
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Makhlouf said the current inflation situation is uncomfortable.

squawks.headline: ECB's Makhlouf says keeping rates on hold does not mean the ECB has finished
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Makhlouf said the decision to hold rates should not be read as a sign that the ECB is done.

squawks.headline: Trump says the Iran war will end very soon, one way or another
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the war with Iran would be over very soon, without giving further detail. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says European representatives will need to take part in Ukraine settlement talks at some point
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said European participation in talks on a peaceful settlement in Ukraine will be required at some stage. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Centcom commander says the Strait of Hormuz transit route has been cleared of sea mines
squawks.detail: The commander of US Central Command said the transit route through the Strait of Hormuz had been cleared of sea mines, and that 1.5 billion barrels of crude had been exported through the strait since the summer. He added that he saw no IRGC presence when he visited the strait earlier this week.

squawks.headline: China's Xi calls the EU a partner and says differences can be resolved through equal dialogue
squawks.detail: Chinese President Xi Jinping said China sees the EU as a partner, according to state broadcaster CCTV. He added that the two sides can always resolve their differences and problems if they keep to that partnership and to equal dialogue.

squawks.headline: BoE surveys show firms expect to raise pay by around 3.5% in 2027, similar to current rates
squawks.detail: Bank of England business surveys released on Friday show firms expect pay growth of around 3.5% next year, broadly in line with current settlements, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Moscow has noted Zelenskyy's stated willingness to discuss territorial issues
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russian officials had heard the Ukrainian president's remarks about being open to talks on territory, following agreement to resume trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia negotiations.

squawks.headline: Qatari mediators are in Tehran to discuss the latest US proposal for peace talks, Axios reports
squawks.detail: Axios reports that Qatari mediators are in Tehran for talks on the latest US peace talks proposal. The report gives no further detail.

squawks.headline: Kremlin calls the Oleshky situation an isolated case that should not be applied to the wider Ukraine settlement process
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the incident in Oleshky should not be taken as representative of the overall peace process in Ukraine.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kocher says inflation risks have risen and action will be needed if the situation does not improve quickly
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Martin Kocher said inflation risks have clearly increased. He added that neither moving too early nor sitting and waiting would secure price stability.

squawks.headline: ECB's Panetta says the price outlook is worsening and further rate rises could prove necessary
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Panetta said inflation is expected to stay above 2% for several quarters and core inflation could rise more sharply early next year. He also said the rise in long-term yields must be taken into account as policy is calibrated, and that the ECB can adjust its stance quickly if the international situation improves or financial tensions weigh on inflation.

squawks.headline: Italian flash October HICP jumps to 5.6% y/y, well above 4.6% forecast and up from 4.2%
squawks.detail: Italy's preliminary October HICP rose 1.2% m/m against a 0.4% forecast. National CPI rose 5.4% y/y against a 4.6% forecast, and 0.9% m/m against a 0.1% forecast.

squawks.headline: Eurozone Q3 GDP grows 0.4% q/q in flash estimate, above 0.2% forecast; annual growth picks up to 1.3%
squawks.detail: The preliminary flash estimate shows euro area GDP up 0.4% q/q, against a 0.2% forecast and down from 0.6% previously. Annual growth is 1.3%, above the 1.1% forecast and up from 1.2%.

squawks.headline: BoE survey finds no sign of an inflation premium in pay awards and limited pass-through of cost pressures to prices
squawks.detail: A Bank of England survey reports no evidence that pay awards include an inflation premium. It also finds that firms are passing only a limited share of cost pressures through to prices.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel says the ECB will act decisively if needed
squawks.detail: Bundesbank President and ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said the central bank is prepared to take decisive action if required. He spoke after earlier saying that a price rise in the coming weeks cannot be ruled out.

squawks.headline: ECB's Nagel sees no significant second-round effects yet but says a price rise in the coming weeks cannot be ruled out
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Nagel said the decision to hold rates had not been easy. He also said medium-term inflation expectations must stay firmly anchored.

squawks.headline: UK Decision Maker Panel puts firms' year-ahead CPI expectations at 3.4% in October
squawks.detail: The October Decision Maker Panel survey of UK businesses shows firms expect CPI inflation of 3.4% over the year ahead.

squawks.headline: Merz to pass Asian partners' concerns over EU 'Made in Europe' protectionism risk on to Brussels
squawks.detail: Reuters reported that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Friday he would take to Brussels concerns from key Asian trading partners that the EU's Made in Europe initiatives could become a new form of protectionism.

squawks.headline: EU carbon price climbs to €90 a tonne, its highest level since January
squawks.detail: A market commentator reported that EU carbon allowances reached €90 per tonne on Friday morning, the first time at that level since January.

squawks.headline: PBOC sets its overnight reverse repo rate at 1.25%; open market operation changes take effect 2 November
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China has set its overnight reverse repo rate at 1.25%. It says the changes to its open market operations take effect on 2 November.

squawks.headline: North Rhine-Westphalia's October CPI slows to 2.7% y/y from 3.3%
squawks.detail: Annual inflation in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's most populous state, slowed to 2.7% in October from 3.3% in September, ahead of the national flash estimate.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says European negotiators' role in US-Ukraine-Russia talks has not been discussed; Putin open to contacts
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said there had been no discussion of European negotiators joining the trilateral talks between the US, Ukraine and Russia. He added that Putin is open to contacts with everyone in pursuit of a peaceful settlement of the conflict in Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Italian Q3 GDP flat q/q in preliminary estimate, below 0.1% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.8%
squawks.detail: Italy's preliminary third-quarter GDP was unchanged on the quarter, against a 0.1% forecast and after 0.2% growth previously. Annual growth eased to 0.8% from 1.0%.

squawks.headline: Bavaria's October CPI slows to 2.8% y/y from 3.2%
squawks.detail: Annual inflation in the German state of Bavaria eased to 2.8% in October from 3.2% the previous month.

squawks.headline: German Q3 GDP grows 0.2% q/q, above 0.1% forecast; annual growth picks up to 1.2%
squawks.detail: Germany's preliminary Q3 GDP rose 0.2% on the quarter against a 0.1% estimate, after 0.3% in the previous quarter. Annual growth came in at 1.2%, above the 1.1% estimate and up from 1.0%.

squawks.headline: Kremlin aide Ushakov says Russia, the US and Ukraine have agreed to resume trilateral negotiations
squawks.detail: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the three countries had agreed to restart trilateral talks, responding to media reports about Europe's possible involvement in the negotiations.

squawks.headline: German unemployment rises by 4k in October, below 5k forecast; jobless rate holds at 6.4% as expected
squawks.detail: German seasonally adjusted unemployment rose by 4k, against a 5k forecast and 12k previously. The unemployment rate was 6.4%, in line with the forecast and unchanged from the previous month.

squawks.headline: Japan's Katayama says the budget process will consider how much surplus the BoJ's ETF sales produce and how to handle it
squawks.detail: Japan's finance minister Katayama said the government would consider the specific amount of surplus from the BoJ's ETF sales, and how to treat it, when drawing up the budget.

squawks.headline: ECB's Rehn says growth and inflation outlook remains highly uncertain and upside inflation risks are still elevated
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn said the outlook for growth and inflation is still very uncertain and that risks of higher inflation remain clearly elevated. He added that policymakers need to stay vigilant about second-round effects.

squawks.headline: Saxony's October CPI slows to 2.8% y/y from 3.4%, with prices down 0.2% m/m
squawks.detail: Figures for the German state of Saxony show annual inflation easing to 2.8% in October from 3.4% the previous month. Prices fell 0.2% m/m, after a 0.6% rise previously; no forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Dutch Q3 GDP grows 0.6% q/q, above 0.3% forecast; annual growth picks up to 2.1%
squawks.detail: Preliminary figures show Dutch GDP grew 0.6% q/q in the third quarter, against a 0.3% forecast and matching the previous quarter's 0.6%. Annual growth came in at 2.1%, compared with a forecast of 1.3% and 1.6% previously.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz says he is working to end the Iran war quickly, citing its heavy impact on Europe
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Merz said the Iran war is having a major impact on Europe and that this is why he is holding intensive talks on his Asia trip. He also said the US is shifting its foreign policy and Germany must do likewise.

squawks.headline: Spanish Q3 GDP grows 0.6% q/q in line with forecast, slowing from 0.7%; annual growth picks up to 2.7%
squawks.detail: Spain's preliminary third-quarter estimate shows 0.6% growth on the quarter, as forecast and down from 0.7% previously. Annual growth is 2.7%, matching the forecast and up from 2.6%.

squawks.headline: Spanish flash October national CPI holds at 4.9% y/y as forecast; monthly rise of 0.6% is below the 0.7% forecast
squawks.detail: Spain's flash national CPI for October is unchanged at 4.9% y/y, in line with forecast. On the month, prices rise 0.6%, against a 0.7% forecast and 0.3% previously.

squawks.headline: Spanish flash October HICP eases to 4.9% y/y, in line with forecast and down from 5.0%; up 0.5% m/m
squawks.detail: Spain's flash October HICP rose 4.9% y/y, matching the 4.9% forecast, after 5.0% the month before. On the month it rose 0.5%, also in line with forecast, after 0.6% previously.

squawks.headline: ECB's Dolenc says the energy shock is not yet feeding broader price pressures but warns inflation may stay above 2% for years
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Dolenc said the energy shock had not yet spread into wider price pressures, but that higher energy prices risk more persistent inflation. He added that inflation could remain above 2% in the coming years.

squawks.headline: French flash October HICP rises 3.8% y/y, above 3.6% forecast and up from 3.4% in September
squawks.detail: France's preliminary October harmonised inflation came in at 3.8% y/y and 0.4% m/m, against forecasts of 3.6% and 0.3%. National CPI rose 3.4% y/y against a 3.3% forecast (previously 3.1%), and 0.4% m/m against a 0.2% forecast (previously -0.3%).

squawks.headline: French producer prices rise 1.7% m/m in September, up from 1.0% the previous month
squawks.detail: French PPI rose 1.7% month on month, compared with 1.0% in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the BoJ is watching spring wage talks closely, which must make 2% inflation built in
squawks.detail: Speaking after the BoJ's policy decision, Governor Ueda said the bank is watching next spring's wage negotiations closely and that annual wage talks need to reach a point where 2% inflation is built in. He added that the BoJ still needs to watch whether the price trend becomes anchored.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says the policy rate is still below neutral and will be adjusted at the right time to stop risks materialising
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said at his post-decision press conference that work remains because the policy rate is below the neutral level. He also said rate adjustments would be timed to prevent risks from materialising.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says he wants to bring the policy rate to a neutral level in an appropriate way
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said this at his press conference after the BoJ held its short-term rate at 1.25%.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda expects faster ETF sales to have only a limited market impact; says upside risks need an appropriate response
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda spoke after the decision to speed up ETF sales. He said the faster pace should have only a limited effect on markets and that the bank must respond appropriately to upside risks.

squawks.headline: China's most-active 30-year government bond futures contract drops 1.00% intraday to 117.34 yuan
squawks.detail: The most-active TL contract on 30-year Chinese government bonds fell 1.00% during the session to 117.34 yuan.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda says a rate rise will be considered at every meeting, the next one included
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said the bank will weigh a rate increase at each policy meeting, including the next one. He spoke after the BoJ held its short-term rate at 1.25%.

squawks.headline: Nationwide UK house prices flat m/m in October against -0.2% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.5%
squawks.detail: Nationwide's October index shows UK house prices unchanged on the month, after -0.2% in September, against a -0.2% forecast. Annual growth (NSA) eases to 0.5% from 0.8%, below the 0.6% forecast.

squawks.headline: German import prices rise 10.4% y/y in September, above 10.3% forecast; up 2.1% m/m
squawks.detail: German import prices rose 10.4% from a year earlier, against a 10.3% forecast and 8.3% previously. On the month they rose 2.1%, against a 2% forecast and 1.0% previously.
